 HSC, equivalent exam pass rate 52.12%, 40,084 secure GPA-5 
 A total of 12,70,583 students appeared in the examinations under 11 education boards across the country. 
 TBS Report 
 31 October, 2026, 11:00 am 
 Last modified: 31 October, 2026, 11:06 am 
 Photo: Rajib Dhar/TBS "> 
 Photo: Rajib Dhar/TBS 
 The pass rate in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations stands at 52.12%, with 40,084 students securing a Grade Point Average (GPA) of 5. 
 The results were published today (31 October), according to the education authorities.
 A total of 12,70,583 students appeared in the examinations under 11 education boards across the country.
 Keep updated, follow The Business Standard's Google news channel
 Of them, 6,21,969 were boys, and 6,48,614 were girls, with 26,645 more girls than boys taking part in the examinations.
 The examinations were held at 2,697 centres across the country, with students from 9,439 educational institutions participating.
 Under the nine general education boards, 10,69,714 students took part in the examinations. The examinations were held under a uniform question paper across these boards.
 The HSC and equivalent examinations began simultaneously across the country on 2 July under nine general education boards, the Bangladesh Technical Education Board and the Bangladesh Madrasah Education Board.
 Although the written examinations were initially scheduled to conclude on 8 August, some examinations under several boards, including Chattogram, were postponed due to natural disasters and floods and held later. The practical examinations were completed by 15 August.
 Meanwhile, students dissatisfied with their results can apply for scrutiny or reassessment of their answer scripts from 1 November.
 According to a press release, students can submit applications online until 7 November. Detailed instructions will be available on the websites of the respective education boards.
